text: In 1946, ads told America: more doctors smoke this cigarette than any other.
The proof? The ads claimed a survey of 113,597 doctors.
But who ran it? Not scientists. The cigarette company's own ad agency.
Its people showed up at medical conventions and doctors' offices.
First, they handed out free cartons.
Then they asked: so... which brand do you smoke?
And medical journals? They were taking cigarette ad money too.
Even JAMA, the doctors' own journal, only stopped in 1953.
The doctors weren't selling cigarettes. The money was.
